title: Algorithm XXXX: Computation of finite element degree-of-freedom transformation matrices
summary: The arithmetic intensity of algorithms for computing finite element operators increases with increasing polynomial degree. This has made high degree methods particularly attractive on modern CPU and GPU architectures, since performance at low degree is limited by memory bandwidth and only a small fraction of the floating point capacity of the processor is used. Higher degree methods can exploit a significantly greater fraction of the available compute power. While stable methods for computing high-degree finite element bases are well-established, there is no universal and automated algorithm…
